questions.question: Which action best represents scientific inquiry?
options: Accepting a claim without checking it
Observing carefully and testing an idea
questions.explanation: Scientific inquiry uses observations, questions and tests to build evidence-based explanations.

questions.question: A student wants to know whether sunlight affects plant growth. What should be changed deliberately?
options: The type of plant in every pot
The amount of water for each plant
The soil and pot size for every plant
questions.explanation: To test sunlight fairly, vary sunlight while keeping other important conditions as similar as possible.

questions.question: Why do scientists repeat an experiment?
options: To make the result look more exciting
To check whether the result is reliable
questions.explanation: Repeated trials help identify errors and show whether a result is consistent.

questions.question: Which feature is commonly used to group plants?
options: Whether they can move from place to place
Whether they make their own food and their body features
questions.explanation: Scientists group plants using observable features such as roots, stems, leaves and ways of reproducing.

questions.question: Which animal is an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: An earthworm has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate.

questions.question: A camel is well suited to desert life mainly because it has features that help it to:
questions.explanation: Camels have adaptations that help them manage heat and scarce water in deserts.

title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

questions.question: Which meal is most likely to be balanced?
options: Only plain rice at every meal
questions.explanation: A balanced meal includes different food groups that supply energy, body-building nutrients and protective nutrients.

questions.question: Which nutrient is especially important for growth and repair of body tissues?
questions.explanation: Proteins help the body grow and repair tissues.

questions.question: Why should we wash our hands before eating?
options: To remove germs and reduce the chance of illness
To remove all nutrients from food
questions.explanation: Handwashing helps prevent harmful germs from entering the body with food.

questions.question: What happens when the north pole of one magnet is brought near the north pole of another?
questions.explanation: Like magnetic poles repel; unlike poles attract.

questions.question: Which object is most likely to be attracted by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron is a magnetic material and is attracted by a magnet.

questions.question: A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest approximately in which direction?
questions.explanation: A freely suspended magnet aligns approximately along the north–south direction.

questions.question: Which is the standard SI unit of length?
questions.explanation: The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length.

questions.question: Which tool is most suitable for measuring the length of a curved line on paper?
options: A flexible thread followed by a ruler
questions.explanation: A thread can follow the curve; its straightened length can then be measured with a ruler.

questions.question: A toy car covers equal distances in equal time intervals. Its motion is:
questions.explanation: Covering equal distances in equal intervals of time is uniform motion.

questions.question: Which property helps us decide whether a material is transparent?
options: Whether light can pass through it clearly
questions.explanation: Transparent materials allow light to pass through so objects can be seen clearly through them.

questions.question: Which material is generally a good choice for making a cooking pot?
questions.explanation: Metals are commonly used for cooking pots because they conduct heat well and can withstand cooking temperatures.

questions.question: A material that dissolves in water is described as:
questions.explanation: A soluble substance forms a solution when it dissolves in water.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer is designed to measure temperature.

questions.question: Why should we not judge temperature only by touching an object?
options: Touch is always more accurate than instruments
Our sense of touch can be misleading
questions.explanation: Touch is subjective and can give misleading impressions; a thermometer provides a measurement.

questions.question: A temperature reading of 30 °C is higher than 20 °C by:
questions.explanation: The difference is 30 − 20 = 10 degrees Celsius.

title: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Liquid water changing into water vapour from the surface is called:
questions.explanation: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapour from its surface.

questions.question: What is condensation?
questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when water vapour cools and changes into liquid water.

questions.question: Why do water droplets form on the outside of a cold glass on a humid day?
options: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold surface
The water inside freezes through the glass
questions.explanation: Airborne water vapour cools at the glass surface and condenses into droplets.

title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

questions.question: Which method can separate stones from rice by hand?
questions.explanation: Handpicking is useful when unwanted pieces are large enough to identify and remove by hand.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to separate insoluble sand from water?
questions.explanation: Filtration traps insoluble sand while water passes through the filter.

questions.question: A mixture of iron filings and sand can be separated using:
options: A sieve with no size difference
questions.explanation: Iron filings are attracted to a magnet, while sand is not.

questions.question: Which characteristic is shared by all living organisms?
options: They all need energy to carry out life processes
questions.explanation: Living organisms require energy for life processes, although they obtain it in different ways.

questions.question: A seed begins to sprout when suitable conditions are available. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Germination is the beginning of growth of a seed into a seedling under suitable conditions.

questions.question: Which observation is evidence that a plant is responding to its surroundings?
questions.explanation: Plant shoots can grow towards light, showing a response to an environmental stimulus.

questions.question: Which of these is a natural resource?
questions.explanation: Sunlight occurs in nature and is a natural resource.

questions.question: Why are forests important for the environment?
options: They only provide places for buildings
They support biodiversity and help maintain ecological balance
questions.explanation: Forests provide habitats, support many species and contribute to soil and water cycles.

questions.question: Which action helps conserve water?
options: Washing a few items under a continuously running hose
questions.explanation: Repairing leaks reduces avoidable water wastage.

questions.question: Which object is at the centre of our Solar System?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the centre of our Solar System.

questions.question: Why does the Moon appear bright in the night sky?
options: It makes its own visible light like the Sun
It is always closer than the Sun by a fixed amount
questions.explanation: The Moon appears bright because its surface reflects sunlight towards Earth.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to observe distant celestial objects in greater detail?
questions.explanation: A telescope collects light from distant objects and helps us observe them.
